Sure! Here’s a quick and tasty way to make an **Indian‑style steak** at home. I’ll give you a simple recipe that uses common spices and a few pantry staples. Feel free to tweak the spice levels to suit your taste. --- ## Quick Indian‑Style Steak Recipe | Step | What to Do | Tips | |------|------------|------| | **1. Choose the cut** | Use a tender cut like ribeye, sirloin, or strip steak (about 1–1.5 cm thick). | If you’re on a budget, flank steak works too—just marinate longer. | | **2. Make the spice rub** | In a bowl mix:
• 1 tsp ground cumin
• 1 tsp ground coriander
• ½ tsp garam masala
• ½ tsp smoked paprika (or regular paprika)
• ¼ tsp cayenne pepper (adjust for heat)
• 1 tsp salt
• ½ tsp black pepper | Add a pinch of turmeric for color if you like. | | **3. Season the steak** | Pat the steak dry with paper towels. Rub the spice mixture all over both sides. Let it sit for 15–20 min at room temp (or refrigerate for up to 24 h for deeper flavor). | A short rest lets the meat reabsorb juices after cooking. | | **4. Prep the pan** | Heat a heavy skillet (cast iron or stainless steel) over high heat until smoking. Add 1 Tbsp oil (vegetable, canola, or ghee). | Ghee gives a buttery, nutty flavor; oil keeps it from burning. | | **5. Sear the steak** | Place the steak in the hot pan. Sear 2–3 min per side for medium‑rare (adjust time for thickness). Flip only once. | Avoid moving it around; let a crust form. | | **6. Finish with aromatics** | Reduce heat to medium. Add 1 minced garlic clove, 1 sliced shallot, and a handful of fresh cilantro leaves. Cook 30 s, then add 1 Tbsp butter (optional). Spoon melted butter over the steak while it rests. | Butter adds richness; cilantro adds freshness. | | **7. Rest & serve** | Remove steak, tent loosely with foil, and let rest 5 min. Slice against the grain. Serve with a squeeze of lime and a side of sautéed onions or a simple cucumber raita. | Resting locks in juices; slicing against the grain makes it tender. | ### Optional “Masala” Sauce (for extra flavor) | Ingredient | Amount | |------------|--------| | 1 Tbsp ghee | | | 1 small onion, finely chopped | | | 1 tsp ginger‑garlic paste | | | 1 tsp ground cumin | | | 1 tsp ground coriander | | | ½ tsp garam masala | | | ½ tsp turmeric | | | 1 cup tomato puree (or crushed tomatoes) | | | ½ cup water or beef broth | | | Salt to taste | | | Fresh cilantro, chopped | | **How to make it:** 1. Melt ghee in a saucepan over medium heat. 2. Add onion, sauté until golden. 3. Stir in ginger‑garlic paste, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and turmeric; cook 1 min. 4. Pour in tomato puree and water/broth; simmer 10 min until slightly thickened. 5. Season with salt, garnish with cilantro. Pour this sauce over the sliced steak or serve it on the side for dipping. --- ## Serving Ideas | Side | Why It Works | |------|--------------| | **Jeera Rice** | Cumin rice pairs beautifully with the steak’s spices. | | **Naan or Roti** | Warm flatbread is perfect for scooping up sauce. | | **Cucumber Raita** | Cool yogurt dip balances the heat. | | **Grilled Vegetables** | Bell peppers, zucchini, or asparagus add color and nutrition. | Enjoy your flavorful, Indian‑style steak! If you’d like a more elaborate recipe or variations (e.g., tandoori‑marinated steak), just let me know.
